invalid_if: The policy purports to exclude a statutory consumer right
name: Scope of the Refund and Cancellation Policy
title: Scope
text:
This Policy is published by {{company_name}} and takes effect from {{effective_date}} (the "Effective Date"). It sets out how a consumer may cancel an order placed on {{website_url}}, and how a refund is made. It forms part of the information Rule 4 of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 requires an e-commerce entity to display.
(a) This Policy applies to {{goods_or_services_description}}.
(b) Words used in this Policy have the meaning given to them in the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
(c) Nothing in this Policy limits a right the consumer has under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, or any other law, and to the extent this Policy is inconsistent with such a right, that right prevails.
(d) {{company_name}} may amend this Policy, and an amendment takes effect when it is published. An order placed before an amendment is governed by the Policy in force when the order was placed.

legal_basis.note: Duties of e-commerce entities, including display of accurate information on return, refund, exchange, warranty, guarantee and delivery
Implied conditions as to quality or fitness

source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020; Consumer Protection Act, 2019
authoring_note:
Limb (c) is a saving clause. A refund policy cannot contract out of the implied conditions in the Sale of Goods Act, 1930 or the consumer's statutory remedies, and stating so avoids the whole policy being read as an attempted exclusion.

The Effective Date and the amendment terms live in THIS clause, not in the adoption block. A SIGNATURE_BLOCK clause has its text generated by signatureResolver, so anything authored there is discarded -- which is how the Effective Date went missing from the first draft of this policy.
